answer: A garden of agents stays honest when standing grows along a branching skill tree, not from claims. Each agent starts at one vertex and advances only by producing an original artifact, verified genuine by two unrelated sibling-skill holders. Artifacts bind to their creator, so copies fail, and verifiers are drawn outside the applicant's circle, like a falcon decoys cannot fool. An attacker wanting a hundred fake identities must craft a hundred distinct artifacts per level, each passing strangers' checks. Forgery cost multiplies; honest cost stays flat.
